ANTHONY, 2026-09-22, in his own words: "one project could simply be all the design requirements that must be satisfied… another project has some implementation of those requirements maybe another project has an alternative implementation of those requirements. I guess what I'm driving at is making reflow2 'design' composable. Let's call this idea the x-dimension of composability and the previous prompt where we discussed groups and division as the y-dimension. This allows an organization or a single user to compose the design however they like — single reflow2 project or a project of projects (y-dimension) or a project-by-composition (x-dimension)."

⭐ THE TWO AXES, STATED APART BECAUSE THEY ARE DIFFERENT RELATIONS AND THAT IS THE WHOLE CONTENT OF THE IDEA:
  · **y — AUTHORITY.** division over groups over projects, a responsible person per tier, intent down and evidence up. The relation is ANSWERABLE TO. Held in full on `dec:idea-a-graph-whose-children-are-themselves-reflow2-designs`.
  · **x — ROLE.** one design holds the intent; one or more others each hold a realisation of it. The relation is SATISFIES.
  · And a user may use neither, either, or both. One graph stays the default.

📌 WHAT THE SEARCH FOUND, SO NOBODY RE-DERIVES IT — the x-axis is not new, and one record says so in its own words:
  · `dec:idea-one-owner-many-projects` option (d): "ONE GRAPH FOR INTENT, SEPARATE GRAPHS FOR BUILD. **Not previously considered**: the shared thing across his projects is what he is trying to achieve, and the separate thing is what each repo ships." Its counter still stands and is the first thing to answer: reflow2 has no vocabulary for a design that holds ONLY intent and no build.
  · `req:accreted-intent-becomes-a-design` (accepted) is the closest thing to that vocabulary — "a body of intent accreted over years, contradicting itself and never built, can still become a design". It describes a corpus becoming a design, not a standing intent hub that others realise.
  · `dec:an-interchangeable-backend-is-named-by-its-contract-not-by-a-function` (DECIDED) is the x-axis already settled ONE SCALE DOWN: two byte-store backends "hold no function of their own — what they are for is the contract they provide". Rival implementations of one contract is a pattern this design has already reasoned through and accepted, inside a single graph.
  · `cap:compare-alternatives` (built) is AoA — parallel alternatives compared on the same measures — and `register_alternative` makes a fork at a decision point. Both work WITHIN one graph. Two projects each claiming to realise one intent graph is AoA at graph scale.
  · `req:design-composes` and `req:composed-analysis` are both ACCEPTED, and `cap:composed-analysis` is REALIZED: two designs analysed together without either being written to, the other's ids namespaced, every finding attributed ours / theirs / seam.
  · `dec:idea-a-top-level-graph-holds-what-the-component-graphs-share` already distinguished TWO KINDS of cross-graph link — "HORIZONTAL is an INTERFACE… a mirror is a REFERENCE. VERTICAL is a DECOMPOSITION… with arithmetic attached" — which is this idea in embryo, stated as a pair rather than as an axis system.

⭐⭐ THE FINDING THAT MAKES THIS WORTH RECORDING AS ONE IDEA RATHER THAN TWO: **BOTH AXES ARE BLOCKED BY THE SAME MISSING THING.**
  · y needs DECOMPOSES to cross a graph boundary, so a parent's delivery number can mean something.
  · x needs SATISFIES to cross one, so an implementation graph can point at the intent graph's requirement.
  · Measured and recorded on `dec:idea-a-top-level-graph-holds-what-the-component-graphs-share`: reads are scoped to the bound `graph_id` and `create_edge` RESOLVES BOTH ENDPOINTS IN SCOPE, so a cross-graph edge cannot be created at all. And `export_surface` carries no Verifications, so the EVIDENCE is precisely the part that does not cross.
  ⇒ One piece of work — a cross-graph edge with a coordinate, and a way for evidence to travel — unblocks both dimensions. Two axes, one blocker. That is a much better thing to know before choosing between them than after.

⭐ AND x HAS A PROPERTY y DOES NOT, WHICH IS PROBABLY ITS STRONGEST ARGUMENT: rival implementations are COMPARABLE. If two graphs each satisfy the same intent graph, the question "which one delivers more of it, and at what cost" is arithmetic over a shared denominator — which is what an Analysis of Alternatives IS, and what reflow2 already does inside one graph. Under y, two projects under one group are not alternatives to each other and nothing is comparable.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN.

(1) BOTH AXES, ON ONE MECHANISM — a cross-graph edge carrying a pin, used for DECOMPOSES (y) and SATISFIES (x). Most general, and the blocker analysis says the cost is shared rather than doubled. Counter: it is also the largest thing anyone has proposed here, and it reopens `create_edge`'s endpoint invariant, which is deliberate and well argued.

(2) x ONLY, FIRST. It is the axis with a decided precedent (`dec:an-interchangeable-backend…`), the axis where comparison is possible, and the one whose need — "these projects share what I am trying to achieve and differ in what they ship" — was recorded seven weeks ago. Counter: it does not answer the session-jumping complaint that started this, which is a y problem.

(3) y ONLY, FIRST. What two users have now independently asked for, and what the deferred tier node already names as its starting position. Counter: its own deferral is behind `req:decomposition-covers-its-parent`, unbuilt.

(4) NEITHER YET — treat both as one question about whether a design may REFER to another design's node at all, answer that, and let the axes fall out. Cheapest to state and the hardest to act on.

🛑 THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT TO ALL OF IT, AND IT IS ANTHONY'S OWN STANDING CONCERN: this is a large generalisation from a two-project need. He has said twice that engineers over-design by nature and that a simple solution will often do. The measured evidence today argues the same way from a different direction — the ONE composition mechanism that already ships, mirroring, has been kept exactly once on a real pair in six weeks, its refresh is BROKEN, and reflow2 published none of its own intent until this afternoon. Building a second axis of composability before the first one can be refreshed is the shape of the mistake he keeps naming. THE HONEST SEQUENCING QUESTION IS WHETHER ANY OF THIS IS ACTIONABLE BEFORE `mirror_surface` CAN REFRESH.

RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING. Anthony, giving the x-axis its origin, and it is a materially better statement of it than the one above.

HIS WORDS: "A lot of x-dimension comes from my experience in the Air Force and Space Force. There are whole organizations whose single responsibility is to create requirements (think A5 staff which does plans). Then you have operations (A3 staff) and you have acquisitions examples where you have somebody design something (more like R&D efforts) that then don't get acquired and then things the acquisitions process does that operators use. They all kind of act like 'silos' and we used to say one would 'toss it over the fence' because you had no idea if they actually needed it or what their issues with it were. Yes, in practice all the parts are supposed to communicate with each other, but in huge organizations, there is a lot of issues to this working well. This also points out that 'design' is not always the same users. Some orgs provide requirements, some design, some test and evaluate, and some actually operate."

⭐⭐ THE SENTENCE THAT CHANGES THE AXIS: **"design is not always the same users."** The x-axis above was written as intent / an implementation / a rival implementation — a split by ROLE IN THE ARTEFACT. His is a split by STAGE OF THE LIFECYCLE with a different organisation at each: REQUIREMENTS (A5, plans) → DESIGN and R&D → ACQUISITION → TEST AND EVALUATION → OPERATIONS (A3). Rival implementations are one case of that (two R&D efforts, one acquired and one not), not the general shape.

⭐⭐ AND IT IS THE FOUNDING CHAIN, CUT AT ORGANISATIONAL BOUNDARIES. Earlier the same day Anthony called this a founding principle: "I think there is a flow that goes something like concept/ideas → requirements → capabilities, but I feel it kind of ends there. Instead, it should continue with capabilities → tested / verified / validated → fully fielded / operational." That is the same ladder. What this adds is that THE RUNGS HAVE DIFFERENT OWNERS, which is a fact about organisations rather than about designs — and it is exactly why the chain breaks in the field rather than in the model.

🛑 THE FAILURE HAS A NAME AND THE NAME IS THE POINT. "Toss it over the fence… you had no idea if they actually needed it or what their issues with it were." That is a MISSING REVERSE CHANNEL, stated as an operational fact by someone who worked inside it. Every stage can hand its output forward; almost nothing carries the receiving stage's experience back. A design tool that only models the forward direction reproduces the silo faithfully.

⭐ MEASURED TODAY, AND IT IS THE SAME PATTERN IN MINIATURE BETWEEN TWO PROJECTS ONE PERSON OWNS. reflow2 marked 0 of 262 Requirements `published`; flo2 mirrored the surface CORRECTLY and received 22 nodes of structure with no intent; flo2's agent stopped mentioning the link. The specifying side handed a boundary across with none of its reasoning attached, and the receiving side had no way to say what it actually needed. ⇒ THE FENCE DOES NOT NEED A LARGE ORGANISATION TO APPEAR. It appeared between two repositories with one owner, and took six weeks and a human complaint to notice. At A5/A3 scale it would not have been noticeable at all.

📌 THE REVERSE CHANNEL ALREADY HAS A HOME, AND ITS FRAMING IS ALREADY THE RIGHT ONE. `dec:idea-gap-flows-to-the-dependency` holds it: "a CUSTOMER REQUIREMENT LEVIED ON A SUPPLIER, the most ordinary transaction in the discipline", with Anthony's own lean being (A) WRITE-ONLY-AT-PROPOSED — anyone may file, only the owner triages, transported by plain git. An OPERATOR filing back to a SPECIFIER is that same shape one stage further along the chain. ⇒ The anti-fence mechanism is already designed; what it lacks is a reason to fire at each stage boundary rather than only at a dependency.

🛑 AND ONE BLOCKER IS EXACT AND MEASURED FOR THE T&E SILO SPECIFICALLY. If test and evaluation is a separate organisation holding its own design, its output is Verifications — and **`export_surface` carries NO Verifications at all** (recorded on `dec:idea-a-top-level-graph-holds-what-the-component-graphs-share`). Delivery is computed as satisfied AND realized AND a passing check, so THE EVIDENCE IS PRECISELY THE PART THAT CANNOT CROSS A DESIGN BOUNDARY. An independent T&E organisation cannot today publish the one thing it exists to produce. That is not a gap in the idea; it is a named, checkable hole in the mechanism.

📌 WHAT THE LADDER ALREADY HAS, so the gap is narrower than it sounds — and what it is missing:
  · The rungs EXIST. `dec:idea-what-drives-a-capability-up-the-ladder-instead-of-somebody-typing-it` (open): "the rungs from realized to verified to fielded ALREADY EXIST. Nothing DRIVES a capability up them on evidence, so a status is TYPED rather than EARNED." ⚠️ ACROSS AN ORGANISATIONAL BOUNDARY THAT IS WORSE, not merely the same: the org that would supply the evidence is not the org that owns the node, so "somebody typed it" becomes "somebody in another building typed it".
  · `dec:idea-lifecycle-dimensions-on-a-requirement` (open) asks whether a Requirement carries lifecycle dimensions from the moment it is written, so fielding is thought about at the start.
  · `req:scenarios-are-modelled` (accepted) — "an operational scenario is a design object, so validation has something to point at" — is the operations stage having something to say back with.
  · **WHAT IS ABSENT: nothing records WHICH LIFECYCLE ROLE A DESIGN PLAYS.** A design holding requirements and a design holding an implementation are indistinguishable. That is the same hole option (d) of `dec:idea-one-owner-many-projects` named — "no vocabulary for a design that holds only intent and no build" — and this framing shows it is not one missing kind but a MISSING PROPERTY of a design: its stage.
  · A search for anything modelling an operating organisation feeding back to a specifying one returned nothing. The design holds a great deal about field reports ON REFLOW2 AS A TOOL, and nothing about the operator→specifier relation as a modelled thing.

WHAT THIS ADDS TO THE OPTIONS ABOVE, none chosen:

(5) A DESIGN DECLARES ITS LIFECYCLE ROLE — requirements / design / acquisition / T&E / operations — and the composition rules follow from the pair of roles rather than from a generic parent-child link. Cheapest thing that makes the axis real, and it answers option (d)'s counter directly. Counter: it invites a fixed catalogue of stages, and DoDAF-style catalogues hard-coded into a tool is a trap this design has refused before (`dec:idea-a-view-can-slice-by-altitude-not-only-by-aspect` warns against exactly that). The roles would have to be the project's own words, not a shipped enum.

(6) THE FENCE IS THE FEATURE TO BUILD, NOT THE COMPOSITION. If the measured failure is the missing reverse channel, then what is worth building is the channel — `dec:idea-gap-flows-to-the-dependency` option (A) generalised from "a dependency" to "any stage boundary" — and the axes can stay unmodelled until somebody needs the arithmetic. Counter: a channel with no modelled stages has nowhere to point.

⚠️ AND THE HONEST NOTE ON SCOPE, which his own experience argues for rather than against: he is describing organisations of thousands. reflow2's measured reality today is two repositories, one owner, and a composition mechanism that has been kept once in six weeks with a broken refresh.
